issues.legal_issue: A summary criminal proceeding over possession must not be used to determine title or the ultimate right to possession, and a reviewing court must confine its examination to the validity of the orders under review.
material_facts: A party initiated a proceeding concerning possession after alleging forcible dispossession and a risk of breach of peace.
The parties had civil suits concerning the same land, including a suit in which an interim injunction had been granted and an objection to it was pending.
The reviewing court considered the history of transfers and disputes over title and directed restoration of possession.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court held that the reviewing court erred by dealing with the revision as though it were an appeal and by considering title and the ultimate right to possession. The relevant possession proceeding concerned possession on the date of the preliminary order and any dispossession within the preceding two months. The Court nevertheless maintained the quashing of the preliminary and attachment orders.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 145(1) and 146(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the inquiry is principally into possession on the date of the preliminary order and any dispossession within two months before that date, not title or the ultimate right to possession. A revision under Sections 397 and 401 is not an appeal. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.possession_criminal_proceeding: A party initiated a criminal proceeding to address a dispute over possession of property.
predicates.reviewing_court_examines_possession_orde: A reviewing court considered the validity of orders made in a proceeding concerning possession.
predicates.title_or_ultimate_possession_is_consider: The reviewing court considered who held title or the ultimate right to possess the property.

issues.definition: When a reviewing court examines orders from a criminal proceeding concerning possession and considers title or the ultimate right to possession, it must confine its examination to the validity of the orders.

issues.legal_issue: The quashing of preliminary and attachment orders in a possession proceeding may be maintained while the parties’ civil disputes over the same property remain for determination by the civil court.
material_facts: The preliminary order and subsequent attachment were made in a criminal proceeding concerning possession of the land.
Both sides had filed civil suits concerning the land, and an interim injunction and an objection to that injunction remained before the civil court.
The High Court quashed the preliminary and attachment orders, and the Supreme Court found that result unassailable in the circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court maintained the quashing of the preliminary order and the attachment order.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Sections 145(1) and 146(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, in the circumstances, left the parties’ dispute and requests for interim relief to the civil court. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.possession_criminal_proceeding: A party initiated a criminal proceeding to address a dispute over possession of property.
predicates.civil_suits_concern_same_property: The parties filed civil suits concerning the same property that was the subject of the criminal proceeding.
predicates.civil_interim_relief_remains_pending: An application or objection concerning interim relief for the property remained to be considered by the civil court.

issues.definition: When a criminal proceeding concerns possession of property, civil suits concern that same property, and civil interim relief remains pending, the preliminary and attachment orders remain quashed.

issues.legal_issue: A civil court considering interim relief over property must decide the application without being influenced by observations or findings made by a reviewing court in the criminal possession proceeding.
material_facts: The parties had civil suits concerning the same property, with interim relief still to be considered by the civil court.
The High Court had made observations and findings while quashing orders in the criminal possession proceeding.
The Supreme Court permitted the parties to approach the civil court and directed it to consider interim relief without influence from those observations or findings.
issues.conclusion: The parties could approach the civil court for appropriate interim relief, and the civil court was to consider the application independently of the High Court’s observations and findings.
issues.legal_principle: The Court directed that the pending civil court proceedings and applications for interim relief be decided independently of observations or findings made in the criminal proceeding. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.civil_interim_relief_is_sought: A party seeks interim relief concerning the property in a civil court.
predicates.reviewing_court_made_property_observatio: A reviewing court made observations or findings about the property while considering the criminal proceeding.

issues.definition: When interim relief concerning property is sought in civil court after a reviewing court has made property-related observations in a criminal possession proceeding, the civil court must consider the relief independently.
